raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#44267 fused dense Qwen3's decode QK-norm, RoPE and KV-cache write into one aiter kernel on ROCm, but only for a KV cache in the activation dtype. With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` every decode layer still runs two `add_rmsnorm_quant` launches, two contiguous copies of the strided q/k views, `rotary_embedding` and the Triton `reshape_and_cache_flash` fp8 write. The aiter kernels that path calls already quantize the cache write with a per-tensor scale.

## Modifications

- `Qwen3Attention.forward` also takes the fused decode path when the NHD cache is `aiter.dtypes.fp8`, the only fp8 dtype aiter's binding accepts (e4m3fn on gfx950, e4m3fnuz on gfx942).
- The kernel gets the layer's own k/v scales: `k_scale_float` / `v_scale_float` from `BaseKVCacheMethod`, a plain float from `load_kv_cache_scales`, or 1.0 when the layer has none. They are cached as CPU tensors on first use, because the kernel reads them on the host and a device tensor would sync inside graph capture; a scale without a host copy raises.
- The mRoPE (Qwen3-VL) kernel shares the gate and gets the same support; it is covered by the unit test, not benchmarked. bf16 caches are unchanged.
- Reached by dense Qwen3 and the models that use its decoder as their language model (Qwen3-VL dense, the Qwen3 variants of InternVL and Intern-S1, MiniCPM-V 4.5, LightOnOCR, Step3-VL-10B, Qwen3-ASR). Qwen3-MoE and Qwen3.5 have their own attention and are not affected.
- `test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` adds fp8-cache cases for both kernels with k/v scales (1, 1), (0.5, 2) and (2, 0.5), checking q, the dequantized K, V against `(v / scale).to(fp8)`, and that no other slot is written. Passing inverted, swapped or unit scales to the kernel fails every case whose scales are not 1.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (attention backend resolves to `aiter`, decode CUDA graphs on). Every server runs `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` with otherwise default args. Baseline is main `132b0f0ae7`.

**Unit test.** `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py`: 6 passed, 64 subtests passed.

**GSM8K**, `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 4096` (chat API, greedy; 1314 questions after the 5 few-shot examples):

| Model | Baseline | This PR | Runs per arm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 0.9495 (0.9444 to 0.9543) | 0.9475 (0.9437 to 0.9566) | 8 |
| Qwen3-14B-FP8 | 0.9559 | 0.9559 | 1 |

One run has a standard error of 0.006. On Qwen3-8B the baseline's own runs span 1 pt, so a single pair says little and both arms ran 8 times: the difference of the means is -0.20 pt, 95% CI [-0.61, +0.21]. lm_eval's 5-shot GSM8K over 13 few-shot seeds gives +0.06 pt, 95% CI [-0.23, +0.36], and teacher-forced decode NLL on the same questions changes by less than 0.12%.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GPU kernel time in one Qwen3-8B decode step at batch 64 (36 layers), torch profiler, CUDA graphs on:

| Kernel | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `aiter::add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` (q_norm, k_norm) | 72 launches, 288.1 µs | |
| contiguous copies of the strided q/k views | 72 launches, 301.1 µs | |
| `rotary_embedding_kernel` | 36 launches, 155.9 µs | |
| `reshape_and_cache_flash` (fp8 KV write) | 36 launches, 155.1 µs | |
| `fused_mrope_rms_kv_kernel<…, fp8e4m3fn>` | | 36 launches, 165.7 µs |

The decode step goes from 6.39 to 5.94 ms. Qwen3-14B-FP8 at batch 8 shows the same swap: 240 launches taking 1039 µs become 40 launches taking 181 µs. With a bf16 cache both trees run the same fused kernel.

`python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts = max(16, 4 × concurrency)`, prefix cache flushed before each run, one benchmark at a time. Median TPOT, two rounds with the GPU assignment swapped, mean of the two.

**Qwen3-8B** (per-round deltas: −1.8 / −4.1 / −7.5 / −7.6 / −3.1% and −2.3 / −5.3 / −8.0 / −7.5 / −4.5%):

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8.941 | 8.758 | −2.0% | +2.2% |
| 8 | 9.443 | 8.999 | −4.7% | +3.2% |
| 32 | 6.473 | 5.973 | −7.7% | +6.1% |
| 64 | 6.870 | 6.351 | −7.6% | +6.3% |
| 128 | 10.210 | 9.819 | −3.8% | +3.5% |

**Qwen3-14B-FP8** (per-round deltas: −3.8 / −6.9 / −8.2 / −6.3 / −3.2% and −3.7 / −7.4 / −7.3 / −5.9 / −6.1%):

| Concurrency | Baseline (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta | Output throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7.038 | 6.775 | −3.7% | +3.8% |
| 8 | 7.667 | 7.119 | −7.2% | +7.3% |
| 32 | 8.509 | 7.848 | −7.8% | +6.8% |
| 64 | 10.312 | 9.685 | −6.1% | +5.4% |
| 128 | 14.166 | 13.506 | −4.7% | +3.9% |

Mean TTFT is within ±3% of the baseline in every cell; prefill does not take the fused path. At concurrency 1 and 8 Qwen3-8B decodes slower than at 32 in both arms on this stack: at batch 8 one bf16 GEMM per layer runs as aiter's Triton `_gemm_a16_w16_kernel` and takes 6.0 ms of the 9.8 ms step, so the relative gain there understates the 0.18 / 0.44 ms saved per step. gfx942 is not measured.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

### PR Pundit review

(Testing PR Pundit Code Review agent. Not all comments may be relevant. This is a one-time automated pass: please address what is useful, no need to request a re-review. Reach out to @peymanr for suggestions and feedback.)

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | Fused fp8 KV scale prefers stale `scale_float` over plain float | `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:151` |
| 2 | 🔵 | Cached fused KV scales never invalidated on scale/weight reload | `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:276` |
| 3 | 🔵 | Tests cover kernel wrapper only, not forward gate or scale wiring | `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py:32` |
| 4 | 🔵 | `_host_kv_scale` duplicates existing `_resolve_fused_scale` helper | `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:146` |

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: Fused fp8 KV scale prefers stale `scale_float` over plain float
`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:151`

`_host_kv_scale` returns `scale_float` before checking the plain-float `scale`, so after `load_kv_cache_scales` rebinds `k_scale`/`v_scale` to new plain floats while leaving `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float` at checkpoint values, the fused write quantizes with the stale float. The aiter backend's descale and unfused write use the new `layer.k_scale`, silently mis-scaling decode-written KV against prefill and reads. Prefer the live plain-float `scale` or verify the pair is consistent.

**Who is affected:** Qwen3 on ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, a quant config that attaches a `BaseKVCacheMethod` (fp8/modelopt/compressed-tensors/quark), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` and `--quantization-param-path`, during decode on the new fused fp8 path.

_Verified by running it._

**Related past reviews:** [#28144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28144) on `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`, [#17773](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17773) on `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`, [#34095](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34095) on `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py`

#### 2. 🔵 Nit: Cached fused KV scales never invalidated on scale/weight reload
`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:276`

`_aiter_fused_kv_scales` caches the host KV scales on the first fused forward and never rebuilds them. `load_kv_cache_scales` is not affected: it runs in `load_model`, before any forward. `update_weights_from_disk` is affected: it reloads into the live model and re-runs `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, which reassigns `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float`. If the reloaded checkpoint has different KV scales, fused decode keeps quantizing K/V with the old scales while the unfused prefill write and the attention descale use the new ones. Consider resetting `_fused_kv_scales` when the scales are reprocessed, or documenting the limitation.

**Who is affected:** Qwen3 on ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and an fp8 KV cache, after an online `update_weights_from_disk` whose checkpoint changes the KV scales (eager mode, or with `recapture_cuda_graph`).

_Verified by running it._

#### 3. 🔵 Nit: Tests cover kernel wrapper only, not forward gate or scale wiring
`test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py:32`

The new tests exercise `aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv` on hand-built fp8 buffers with scales they construct, and `_host_kv_scale` on its own. Nothing covers the `forward()` dtype gate (`k_cache.dtype in (hidden_states.dtype, aiter_dtypes.fp8)`) or how `_aiter_fused_kv_scales` reads and caches `attn.k_scale`/`k_scale_float`. So a regression in that wiring (swapped k/v, wrong source, fp8 dropped from the gate) would not fail any test. `test_rope_nhd_fp8_cache`/`test_mrope_nhd_fp8_cache` nearly duplicate the bf16 tests and could be folded into them as a dtype/scales subTest loop. A small test through `Qwen3Attention` with preset RadixAttention scales would close the gap.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers relying on CI to catch regressions in the fp8 KV-scale wiring of the Qwen3 aiter fused decode path (ROCm, SGLANG_USE_AITER=1, fp8 KV cache).

_Verified by running it._

#### 4. 🔵 Nit: `_host_kv_scale` duplicates existing `_resolve_fused_scale` helper
`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:146`

`_host_kv_scale` reimplements `_resolve_fused_scale` in memory_pool.py, which already resolves the same per-tensor KV scales (plain float, CPU 0-d tensor, device scalar paired with `*_scale_float`) for the pool's fp8 fused write. A thin wrapper mapping missing scale to 1.0 and raising the capture `ValueError` could reuse the existing helper instead of a parallel implementation. Consolidate to one resolver.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers of the KV-scale resolution logic; no runtime behaviour differs for scales set by `BaseKVCacheMethod` or `load_kv_cache_scales`.

<sub>Shared from a pilot of [PR Pundit](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/pr_pundit), an agentic code reviewer that builds and tests the change and reads the project's past reviews. Reviewed at `678f4b30`; findings checked and posted by @peymanr; points already raised on this PR are left out.</sub>

LGTM. The FP8 path passes the per-layer K/V scales without adding a device-to-host read during graph capture, and the existing BF16/fallback paths are preserved. Please keep the numerical tests with non-unit scales; gfx942 still needs CI coverage.

@@ -52,6 +52,8 @@
 _has_fused_qk_norm_mrope = False
 _has_fused_qk_norm_rope = False
 if _use_aiter:
+    from aiter import dtypes as aiter_dtypes
+
     try:
         from aiter import fused_qk_norm_mrope_3d_cache_pts_quant_shuffle
 
@@ -93,8 +95,10 @@ def aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv(
 
     ``qkv`` is the (num_tokens, (num_heads + 2 * num_kv_heads) * head_dim) QKV
     projection; ``k_cache`` / ``v_cache`` are the NHD (slots, num_kv_heads,
-    head_dim) pool buffers. ``k_scale`` / ``v_scale`` must be CPU tensors: the
-    kernel reads them on the host. Returns q as (num_tokens, num_heads * head_dim).
+    head_dim) pool buffers, in ``qkv``'s dtype or ``aiter.dtypes.fp8``. An fp8
+    cache stores k / k_scale and v / v_scale; other caches ignore the scales.
+    ``k_scale`` / ``v_scale`` must be CPU tensors: the kernel reads them on the
+    host. Returns q as (num_tokens, num_heads * head_dim).
     """
     num_tokens = qkv.shape[0]
     q_out = torch.empty(
@@ -139,6 +143,23 @@ def aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv(
     return q_out.view(num_tokens, -1)
 
 
+def _host_kv_scale(scale, scale_float) -> float:
+    """Host value of a RadixAttention per-tensor KV scale. ``BaseKVCacheMethod``
+    pairs its device scale with a float, ``load_kv_cache_scales`` sets a plain
+    float, and without a scale the pool writes unscaled."""
+    if scale is None:
+        return 1.0
+    if scale_float is not None:
+        return float(scale_float)
+    if isinstance(scale, (int, float)):
+        return float(scale)
+    # Reading it here would be a device-to-host sync, which graph capture forbids.
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"the fused KV write needs a host copy of the KV scale, got a "
+        f"{type(scale).__name__} without one"
+    )
+
+
 class Qwen3Attention(nn.Module):
     def __init__(
         self,
@@ -245,13 +266,23 @@ def __init__(
             and self.head_dim in (64, 128, 256, 512)
             and self.q_norm.variance_epsilon == self.k_norm.variance_epsilon
         )
-        if self.use_fused_qk_norm_mrope or self.use_fused_qk_norm_rope:
-            # Scale tensors MUST stay on CPU: the C++ kernel uses .item<float>()
-            # which triggers hipMemcpy D2H + sync on CUDA tensors, breaking graph capture.
-            # Explicit device='cpu' is required because SGLang constructs models inside
-            # a `with torch.device('cuda'):` context that changes the default device.
-            self._fused_k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="cpu")
-            self._fused_v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="cpu")
+        # Built on first use: the KV scales are set after __init__, by
+        # process_weights_after_loading or load_kv_cache_scales.
+        self._fused_kv_scales: Optional[Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]] = None
+
+    def _aiter_fused_kv_scales(self) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """(k_scale, v_scale) for the fused KV write as CPU float32 tensors. The
+        kernel reads them on the host at launch, so a device tensor would sync
+        and break graph capture, and a captured graph keeps the values it was
+        captured with."""
+        if self._fused_kv_scales is None:
+            k_scale = _host_kv_scale(self.attn.k_scale, self.attn.k_scale_float)
+            v_scale = _host_kv_scale(self.attn.v_scale, self.attn.v_scale_float)

### PR Pundit review

(Testing PR Pundit Code Review agent. Not all comments may be relevant. This is a one-time automated pass: please address what is useful, no need to request a re-review. Reach out to @peymanr for suggestions and feedback.)

| # | | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🟠 | Fused fp8 KV scale prefers stale `scale_float` over plain float | `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:151` |
| 2 | 🔵 | Cached fused KV scales never invalidated on scale/weight reload | `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:276` |
| 3 | 🔵 | Tests cover kernel wrapper only, not forward gate or scale wiring | `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py:32` |
| 4 | 🔵 | `_host_kv_scale` duplicates existing `_resolve_fused_scale` helper | `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:146` |

#### 1. 🟠 Should fix: Fused fp8 KV scale prefers stale `scale_float` over plain float
`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:151`

`_host_kv_scale` returns `scale_float` before checking the plain-float `scale`, so after `load_kv_cache_scales` rebinds `k_scale`/`v_scale` to new plain floats while leaving `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float` at checkpoint values, the fused write quantizes with the stale float. The aiter backend's descale and unfused write use the new `layer.k_scale`, silently mis-scaling decode-written KV against prefill and reads. Prefer the live plain-float `scale` or verify the pair is consistent.

**Who is affected:** Qwen3 on ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, a quant config that attaches a `BaseKVCacheMethod` (fp8/modelopt/compressed-tensors/quark), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` and `--quantization-param-path`, during decode on the new fused fp8 path.

_Verified by running it._

**Related past reviews:** [#28144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28144) on `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`, [#17773](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17773) on `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`, [#34095](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34095) on `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py`

#### 2. 🔵 Nit: Cached fused KV scales never invalidated on scale/weight reload
`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:276`

`_aiter_fused_kv_scales` caches the host KV scales on the first fused forward and never rebuilds them. `load_kv_cache_scales` is not affected: it runs in `load_model`, before any forward. `update_weights_from_disk` is affected: it reloads into the live model and re-runs `BaseKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, which reassigns `k_scale_float`/`v_scale_float`. If the reloaded checkpoint has different KV scales, fused decode keeps quantizing K/V with the old scales while the unfused prefill write and the attention descale use the new ones. Consider resetting `_fused_kv_scales` when the scales are reprocessed, or documenting the limitation.

**Who is affected:** Qwen3 on ROCm with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and an fp8 KV cache, after an online `update_weights_from_disk` whose checkpoint changes the KV scales (eager mode, or with `recapture_cuda_graph`).

_Verified by running it._

#### 3. 🔵 Nit: Tests cover kernel wrapper only, not forward gate or scale wiring
`test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope.py:32`

The new tests exercise `aiter_fused_qk_norm_rope_set_kv` on hand-built fp8 buffers with scales they construct, and `_host_kv_scale` on its own. Nothing covers the `forward()` dtype gate (`k_cache.dtype in (hidden_states.dtype, aiter_dtypes.fp8)`) or how `_aiter_fused_kv_scales` reads and caches `attn.k_scale`/`k_scale_float`. So a regression in that wiring (swapped k/v, wrong source, fp8 dropped from the gate) would not fail any test. `test_rope_nhd_fp8_cache`/`test_mrope_nhd_fp8_cache` nearly duplicate the bf16 tests and could be folded into them as a dtype/scales subTest loop. A small test through `Qwen3Attention` with preset RadixAttention scales would close the gap.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers relying on CI to catch regressions in the fp8 KV-scale wiring of the Qwen3 aiter fused decode path (ROCm, SGLANG_USE_AITER=1, fp8 KV cache).

_Verified by running it._

#### 4. 🔵 Nit: `_host_kv_scale` duplicates existing `_resolve_fused_scale` helper
`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py:146`

`_host_kv_scale` reimplements `_resolve_fused_scale` in memory_pool.py, which already resolves the same per-tensor KV scales (plain float, CPU 0-d tensor, device scalar paired with `*_scale_float`) for the pool's fp8 fused write. A thin wrapper mapping missing scale to 1.0 and raising the capture `ValueError` could reuse the existing helper instead of a parallel implementation. Consolidate to one resolver.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers of the KV-scale resolution logic; no runtime behaviour differs for scales set by `BaseKVCacheMethod` or `load_kv_cache_scales`.
